 Watch live Summary
 Storm Boelo is bringing flooding, travel disruption, and power cuts across the UK - here's the latest forecast 
 More than 80,000 customers across Great Britain were without power this morning, and there are also power cuts across the island of Ireland 
 Video from Largs, in Ayrshire, showed water flowing through the town centre - while the tracks were submerged at Dalmarnock station in Glasgow 
 On the railways, people are being told not to travel north of Preston - while on the East Coast, LNER advises against travel north of Edinburgh
 A number of flights across the Irish Sea have been cancelled, while many ferry services are also suspended
 Amber warnings for wind remain in place across large parts of Scotland and northern England , with a range of events cancelled 
 And it's not just wind and rain - there is snow in the Cairngorms , with the local rescue team saying winter has "well and truly" arrived

 Rail replacement coaches are a sign spooky season has arrived published at 12:39 GMT 12:39 GMT 
 Adam Goldsmith 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Adam Goldsmith Halloween might be approaching, but I challenge
you to find three words more frightening than 'rail replacement bus'. 
 My girlfriend and I woke up to bad news straight
away this morning, when we found out the second part of our journey to York
would need to be completed on a coach from Wakefield.
 After nonetheless clambering aboard a packed
train at King's Cross, things have since taken a turn for the worse, as we now
find ourselves stuck outside Retford.
 Our train manager tells us a tree has fallen on
the line near Doncaster, and - as she put it - "to add to our woes" there
are issues with the overhead lines.
 Our Sunday lunch booking in York is looking
increasingly precarious. Let's see if we make it.

 Recap: Tens of thousands without power as Storm Boelo brings widespread disruption published at 12:24 GMT 12:24 GMT 
 Katie Williams 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images Storm Boelo battered parts of the UK overnight with top wind speeds of 85mph recorded. 
 Tens of thousands are without power, with more than 80,000 customers affected earlier this morning, according to the Energy Networks Association . 
 Meanwhile, fallen trees and flooding have wreaked havoc with parts of the train and road networks, with people being told not to travel north of Preston on some lines . 
 In Scotland, sections of two motorways were closed earlier. They have since reopened but several A-roads and bridges remain closed, according to Traffic Scotland. 
 There have also been flight and ferry cancellations over the Irish Sea.
 Conditions overnight caused chaos in some areas, with rubbish littering the streets in Renfrew after the River Clyde burst its banks. Video footage from Ayrshire shows one town centre flooding .
 Attractions remain closed in several areas and events have been postponed due to the ongoing wet and windy weather. 
 As of 12:00 GMT, three Met Office weather warnings are still in place including an amber wind warning over most of Scotland.

 Two expired, four still in place: Latest Met Office weather warnings published at 12:08 GMT 12:08 GMT 
 Image source, Met Office While two weather warnings for Northern Ireland - one amber and one yellow each for wind - now lifted, there's still three Met Office warnings in place:
 A yellow rain warning over parts of northern Scotland is in place until 15:00 
 An amber wind warning over most of Scotland and parts of northern England will end at 21:00
 A yellow wind warning over Scotland and parts of northern England, the west midlands and north Wales also ends at 21:00
 One further warning - a yellow rain warning stretching from parts of the north of England to the south, and across Wales - was also in place for the storm but expired at 23:00 BST last night.

 Yellow wind warning lifts over Northern Ireland published at 12:00 GMT 12:00 GMT Breaking 
 It's now 12:00 GMT which means the yellow wind warning covering Northern Ireland has now lifted.
 Despite the warning lifting, parts of the nation are still forecast to experience wet and windy conditions over the coming hours, according to the Met Office weather forecast map.
 We'll have more on the three remaining Met Office warnings over Scotland, parts of northern England and north Wales in our next post.

 Thousands of homes in Northern Ireland are without power after Storm Boelo published at 11:55 GMT 11:55 GMT 
 Holly Fleck 
BBC News Northern Ireland 
 About 41,000 homes, farms and businesses across the Republic of Ireland are without electricity.
 Northern Ireland Electricity said 7,000 customers have been affected, with the worst impacted areas including Springfield in County Fermanagh and Bushmills in County Antrim, where more than 1,000 homes near each village are without power.
 A spokesperson for the Republic of Ireland's ESB Networks says properties in the north-west of the country are primarily affected.
 "As Met Éireann weather warnings remain in place, there may be further power outages this morning," they said.
 Among the villages worst affected in the Republic of Ireland is Milford in County Donegal with more 1,600 homes without power and Aghagad in County Sligo with over 1,200 homes impacted.
 ESB Networks says crews have been deployed to all impacted areas and they "expect the vast majority of impacted customers to have their supply restored by this evening".
 Image source, Tartan eyes / BBC Weather Watchers Image caption, It has been a wet and windy weekend in Northern Ireland - this picture was taken this morning in Ballygally

 Several Irish Ferries services cancelled today published at 11:45 GMT 11:45 GMT 
 Multiple ferry services run by Irish Ferries are cancelled today because of the weather conditions.
 A Holyhead to Dublin service scheduled for 13:15 GMT has been cancelled as were two others earlier this morning. Another two early morning services between Dublin and Holyhead also didn't sail.
 The 16:30 ferry from Cherbourg in France to Dublin has also been cancelled.
 Image source, PA

 Scottish ferry operator says almost all services are disrupted published at 11:36 GMT 11:36 GMT 
 Image source, PA Media Image caption, A sign at the terminal at Wemyss Bay earlier today
 CalMac says 27 out of 30 services on its Scottish west coast ferry network are affected by bad weather.
 Cancelled services include Ullapool to Stornoway and Mallaig to the Small Isles. 
 The ferry operator warns that some routes could face disruption until Monday and cancellation at short notice.

 Storm Boelo floods town centre of Largs, Ayrshire published at 11:27 GMT 11:27 GMT 
 The town centre of Largs, a coastal town west of Glasgow, completely flooded last night.
 The owner of Geraldo's, an ice cream shop on the high street, says it's the highest she has seen the water rise in her 36 years there.

 A wild night in the Highlands - I think I'll stay in today published at 11:18 GMT 11:18 GMT 
 Imogen James 
Reporting from Inverness 
 The picture near Inverness this morning is bleak. 
 The wind howled overnight and my garden flooded this morning. 
 Several trees are down blocking vital local roads, and the winds continue to blow strongly with no sign of slowing down. 
 Traffic is noticeably quieter, unsurprisingly. 
 After feeding my dogs this morning, the feed bowls went in the wind. 
 Inverness Airport has some cancellations and the Kessock Bridge into the city is closed to high sided vehicles. 
 I think I’ll stay in today.

 Bursting banks of River Clyde causes chaos in Renfrew published at 11:07 GMT 11:07 GMT 
 Mike Farrell 
BBC Scotland 
 Dramatic images shared on social media last night showed the River Clyde bursting its southern banks in Renfrew.
 This morning the water has subsided, but the impact can be seen all through the town. The water has come up leaving rubbish strewn across the street.
 Cars have been moved and dumped onto pavements. Bins have been upended and dumped across the street – a familiar sight in weather like this.
 Local businesses, including the Foundry Gym, have posted about having to close due to flooding.
 It was still wet and windy out there this morning as I walked around the town.

 Scotland's rail and roads flooded by Storm Boelo published at 10:57 GMT 10:57 GMT 
 Steven McKenzie and Craig Williams 
BBC Scotland 
 Image source, Network Rail Scotland Image caption, Flooding at Dalmarnock station in Glasgow
 ScotRail has updated its travel advice on how services are being affected by Storm Boelo, and it’s not good news. The operator says speed restrictions will be on all routes, all day - meaning longer journey times and some service alterations.
 The following routes are closed or facing cancellations:
 Glasgow Central - Ayr: No trains operating between Kilwinning and Ayr
 Glasgow Queen Street - Oban / Mallaig: No trains between Fort William and Mallaig and between Crianlarich and Oban
 Inverness - Kyle of Lochalsh: No trains between Kyle of Lochalsh and Achnashellach
 Inverness - Wick / Thurso : No trains between Helmsdale and Wick / Thurso
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The A82 blocked at Dumbuck Quarry due to flooding on Sunday in Dumbarton, 13km from Glasgow
 Highland Council says a number of roads in the area are affected, including the A832 between Fortrose and Rosemarkie and A890 at Ardnarff, south of Strathcaron.
 Trees are also down on the road between Cardross and Alexandria in Argyll and Bute.

 We can now bring you some more pictures from Scotland, which continues to experience wet and windy conditions along with much of the north of the UK.
 Weather warnings remain in place today as Storm Boelo continues to disrupt travel and leave tens of thousands without power.

 Almost 83,000 still without power across Britain published at 10:39 GMT 10:39 GMT Breaking 
 The Energy Networks Association (ENA) says that, as of 08:00 GMT, 82,600 customers are without power in Great Britain as Storm Boelo continues to cause widespread disruption to the power network. 
 It adds that 344,900
 customers have been reconnected following Storm Austen - which hit on Friday - and Boelo.
 It says severe weather is limiting engineers' ability to safely start restoration work in some places.
 For context: ENA is the industry body representing the companies which
operate the energy networks in the UK and Ireland

 Flights and ferries cancelled in Belfast published at 10:35 GMT 10:35 GMT 
 Holly Fleck 
BBC News NI 
 At Belfast City Airport, flights departing for Edinburgh, Cardiff, Manchester and Kirkwall on Sunday morning have been cancelled.
 Meanwhile, flights arriving from Edinburgh, Leeds Bradford, Cardiff, Manchester, Birmingham and Inverness have also been cancelled. At Belfast International Airport, 17 flights have been cancelled this morning. 
 "Storm Boelo continues to cause some disruption to flights today. Please check with your airline for latest flight information as delays can be expected," a spokesperson says.
 At Dublin Airport, strong winds continue to have an impact on flight operations on Sunday.
 "Mainly due to weather issues in other countries, airlines have so far cancelled 12 inbound and 12 outbound flights," Graeme McQueen from the airport's operator DAA says.
 He advises passengers to travel to the airport as normal and keep in contact with their airline, adding that further disruption is possible due to the wind warnings.

 Hundreds of homes without power in Wales published at 10:27 GMT 10:27 GMT 
 Angela Ferguson 
BBC News Wales 
 Hundreds of homes are without power in Wales this morning after back-to-back storms led to flooding and felled trees across the country.
 Wind gusts of 84mph were recorded in Capel Curig, Conwy County, which also saw two inches of rainfall.
 Four flood warnings remain in place in South Wales, while 555 homes in Powys are without power. SP Energy says it is dealing with 14 power outages in north and mid-Wales.
 Other parts of Wales are still recovering from the previous storm, Austen.
 Staff at the Tafell a Tân cafe in Ceredigion have thanked the community for helping with a clean-up operation after the venue was forced to close on Friday due to a sandstorm.
 Image caption, Volunteers help clean up Tafell a Tân cafe after a sandstorm caused by Storm Austen.

 Hurling championship postponed in Ballycastle, Knowsley Safari Park closed published at 10:19 GMT 10:19 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The Common Eland antelopes at Knowsley Safari Park won't have any visitors on Sunday
 It's not just travel that Storm Boelo is disrupting. Events across the UK have been cancelled or postponed due to the weather conditions, including:
 A Halloween family fun day at Dean Park Castle and Country Park in Kilmarnock, Ayrshire scheduled for Sunday, has been postponed
 The Antrim Senior Hurling Championship final , which was supposed to be today in Ballycastle , has been postponed until 1 November
 Meanwhile Northamptonshire Day in Kettering , which celebrates the county's heritage, has also been postponed
 Knowsley Safari Park in Merseyside announced the site will be closed on Sunday "due to high winds", while Liverpool Cathedral is closed and Aintree racing has been cancelled
 Clifford's Tower, the Yorkshire Museum and Museum Gardens in York are also all closed due to the weather

 Dover-Calais ferries cancelled due to storm published at 10:07 GMT 10:07 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters Two ferry services between Dover and Calais are cancelled due to the weather, according to operator DFDS.
 The Danish ferry company says that customers booked onto its 10:40 GMT service from Dover and its 14:20 GMT service from Calais will be transferred to the first available departure. 
 As we reported earlier, some ferry services in Scotland and Northern Ireland have also been cancelled because of the storm.

 Amber wind warning expires in Northern Ireland published at 10:00 GMT 10:00 GMT Breaking 
 The amber wind warnings covering County Antrim and County Londonderry have now expired. 
 Storm Boelo's strongest winds were expected there on Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
 You can see all the weather warnings across the UK in our earlier post here.

 Roads closed in Northern Ireland due to fallen trees published at 09:54 GMT 09:54 GMT 
 Ralph Hewitt 
BBC News NI 
 Image source, PA Media A number of roads across Northern Ireland are closed due to fallen trees, says the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI).
 The Ballyrobin Road in County Antrim is currently impassable after the junction with the Seven Mile Straight, which may affect journeys to Belfast International Airport.
 The Glenshane Road in County Londonderry, about half a mile from the Castledawson roundabout, is also impassable.
 The PSNI is urging road users to exercise caution.
 "If travel is essential, leave extra time for your journey and increase your stopping distance from the car in front," it adds
